findings.finding: No blocking static rendering or report-state inconsistency was observed across the six required control checkpoints.
findings.pixel_evidence: All six originals show the hero, companion, ore, textured terrain and trial HUD. Individual observations and original state windows are listed per image.
findings.state_evidence: HP17 is 500 initially, 476 after six held-mining impacts; reset restores 500 and resets=1; touch mining leaves 492 and impact_serial=8. Keyboard release position is identical at frames 430/490; touch release position is identical at 780/840, with mining=false.
findings.likely_cause: The existing candidate renders the trial fixture and responds to the exercised controls; no defect cause is inferred.
findings.uncertainty: A static appearance cannot independently prove HP changes, input timing or all animation phases; those conclusions use the recorded state report. No approved-target fidelity comparison or broader production coverage was performed.
findings.smallest_next_step: Bind these reviewed bytes in the existing small review gate and proceed only with the already authorized additive trial workflow and its 27-file public verification.

findings.finding: These are six asynchronous control checkpoints, not a motion-quality sequence.
findings.pixel_evidence: The touch-mining image is a post-release pose; report mining=false at both frames 645 and 655. No image is assigned an exact impact frame.
findings.state_evidence: CDP captures take 114–171 ms and are bracketed by state counters 9 or 10 frames apart. Telemetry elapsed_ms is local to labeled waits; no global synchronized capture timestamp is supplied.
findings.likely_cause: The harness captures control checkpoints through CDP while the game continues running.
findings.uncertainty: Continuous playback, return clearance throughout a cycle, timing smoothness, physical iPhone behavior, sustained FPS and a numeric animation score remain unverified.
findings.smallest_next_step: Keep production acceptance open; use the additive trial for the intended iPhone user check. Do not rerun the unchanged Mac suite to turn these stills into motion evidence.

findings.finding: The upper-left instruction says HUGG while the visible lower-right action control is labeled MINE.
findings.pixel_evidence: Visible in all six 844×390 originals: instruction near x12,y38 and button label near x729,y354.
findings.state_evidence: Touch interaction nevertheless produces two recorded impacts before release.
findings.likely_cause: Likely mixed wording between the trial hint and existing action control; this is an inference from the pixels, not a source diagnosis.
findings.uncertainty: Possible first-use hesitation was not measured and does not block the narrow supervised trial.
findings.smallest_next_step: If the user reports confusion, align the hint/control wording in a separate minimal revision; do not rebuild this passing package for the review.

publisher_review.basis: Source inspection only; publisher and public-byte verification were not executed by this critic.
checks: reviewed() pins DEV13 source, both baseline file sets, dev/worn destination, review flags, exact bundle/baseline/report SHA256s, source identity, passing six-check report and exact nine-file tested manifest.
Base PCK equals pinned DEV13 PCK. The seven files other than index.html/index.pck are required to equal DEV13.
prepare() fetches and verifies size/SHA256 for all 18 existing LIVE/DEV13 files before creating a staging tree; it retains rollback bytes.
Each ordered delta part, the assembled delta and all nine reconstructed candidate files are verified against pinned identities.
The staging file set is exactly 9 LIVE, 9 DEV13, 9 dev/worn files and .nojekyll; the 18 baseline files are rechecked after copying.
Workflow serializes Pages work, makes deployment depend on gated packaging and runs verify afterward. verify() checks exact size/SHA256 of all 27 public game files before recording success.
publisher_review.remaining_uncertainty: No staging/deployment/public receipt is asserted here. Post-deployment verification is required; the workflow retains rollback files but does not automatically roll back a failed public verification.
